payload.goal: Turn round-1 benchmark evidence into an industry-leading sofar release. Waves 1-3 of the combined improvement plan (bench-refresh note 2026-09-15): correctness and quick wins, less bookkeeping and leaner context, a quick-work lane for ad-hoc fixes, and new capabilities (verification-gated drive, decision counters, relevant-lessons injection). Every fix states its predicted gain before it is built (bench-refresh D10) and ships only if round 2's held-out lead margin over the best current competitor holds or grows (D19). Built on branch r1-fixes in its own worktree; round 1 stays on the pinned 0.32.0 install (D5).

PREDICT: Codex S1 −13 tool calls; Codex and Cursor make a project initiative WITH a plan in ≥2/3 reps.

Formatter defence: doctor check and fix for Biome (plus Prettier and markdownlint hazards); write .mcp.json in a formatter-friendly shape (init.ts:1118). PREDICT: agent edits to biome.json or .mcp.json reformatting 3/7 → 0.
stdin/file input for `sofar remember` and `sofar event --payload`, quoted-heredoc examples, `remember --supersedes`. PREDICT: shell-mangling corrections → 0.
Drive diagnostics: carry the adapter's stderr tail, failure or spawn error into the stall note (drive.ts:776, adapter exit record). PREDICT: every launch failure names its cause.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Wave 2: less bookkeeping, leaner context

tasks.title: Next D/M ids in the digest; drop the standing-constraint echo from update_task responses; batch task updates into end_session; MCP server instructions to load core tools in one ToolSearch. PREDICT: sofar share of tool calls 32–38% → ≤20%, −3 to −5 turns per session.
Deduplicate the digest (rejected approaches vs decision `over` text; constraints vs rules), index-first ≤6k chars with details on demand. PREDICT: S2+ digest −25% chars, no C2/C3 loss.
Cache-stable layout: static prefix first, no volatile values at the top, changing reminders late via UserPromptSubmit. PREDICT: cache-creation tokens per session −15%.
Tool surface: trim descriptions (repeated `initiative` text in ~10 tools); review, close and find CLI-first. PREDICT: MCP schemas 14.8k → ≤8k chars.

Automatic capture through hooks: commits (task-id prefix), test pass/fail, files, errors recorded deterministically from PostToolUse/Stop; the model logs only why. PREDICT: sofar MCP/CLI calls per session −40%.

Quick-work lane: ad-hoc fixes land in a standing per-repo maintenance record with no `sofar new`/plan ceremony, auto-captured by hooks, plus one line of why only when a decision was made; promote to an initiative when it grows. PREDICT: overhead ratio on 1–3 minute fixes ≤ 15% of task tokens with the fix recalled later.
Verification-gated drive: run the task's acceptance command before accepting task_done; failures go into the next handoff. PREDICT: drive final pass rate +5 pts over round-1 drive.
Decision counters plus supersession/valid_until so stale decisions leave the digest without a model. PREDICT: C3 no worse at −10% digest.
Relevant-lessons injection: keyword/BM25 match of rejected approaches and past failures at UserPromptSubmit, no model. PREDICT: C3 +5 pts.
Fold in round 1's own loss-study rows (bench-refresh 4.1) as added tasks, each with a predicted gain
Release candidate: full test suite, SPEC acceptance criteria, then the run owner publishes to npm
Hand the release to bench-refresh round 2, with the quick-work addendum chain frozen before it runs

payload.text:
Wave 1 session 2026-09-15 (1.1 + 1.2). Evidence for round-2 checks:
- 1.1: SessionStart in an init-ed repo with no initiative now injects ~560 chars (Session line + new→start→plan). Round-1 Claude S1 injected 0. Check in round 2: S1 turns vs round 1 (predicted −3 to −4) and sessions per S1 record (predicted 1, no minted ulid beside the hook id).
- 1.2: repro on the unfixed build: 12 concurrent `sofar event post-tool` processes with one new session id → 12 session_started. Fixed: 1 (5 runs at N=12; N=40 → 1 start, 40 touches, 226 ms wall, 0 locks left). Check in round 2: grep -c session_started per session id in cursor cells (predicted 0 duplicates).
- Could not attribute round-1's 4 cursor duplicates to hook race vs CLI re-run without reading round-1 cells (off-limits). Both paths are now idempotent, so the prediction holds either way.
- Fresh worktree needs `npm ci` and `npm run build` before the suite: dist/ is gitignored, and spawn-based tests read packages/engine/dist/cli.js.

A fresh git worktree of this repo has no node_modules and no packages/engine/dist (gitignored). Run `npm ci` then `npm run build` before `npm test`. Otherwise `npx vitest` fetches a mismatched vitest and fails to load vitest.config.ts, and spawn-based suites fail because they execute dist/cli.js.

payload.because: Round 1's CLI agents lost turns to shell quoting: apostrophes and inner quotes inside `--payload '<json>'` and `remember "<fact>"` broke the command and produced correction events. stdin under a quoted heredoc is the one shell form that carries any byte unchanged, and the payload reference already pins every example to validate, so the fix is the transport, not the parser. Supersession lets an outdated fact be replaced without a correction event that leaves doctor nagging for both.
payload.chose: 1.5 input forms: `sofar event append --payload` and `sofar remember [text]` each accept the JSON/text three ways — inline as today, `-` for stdin (the quoted-heredoc form the AGENTS block now shows: `--payload - <<'EOF' … EOF`), and `@<path>` for a file; with the value omitted and stdin piped, stdin is read. `remember --supersedes <M-handle>` records `supersedes` on memory_promoted as the QUALIFIED handle `<slug> M<n>` (a bare `M<n>` resolves against the target initiative; either form is validated to name an existing memory before the append). Fold marks the superseded memory (`superseded_by`) within its own record; memory.md renders it struck with the successor named; doctor's repo-memory axis stops nagging for a superseded memory across every record and nags for its successor instead. sofar_remember gains the same `supersedes` arg.
payload.over: (a) a separate `--payload-file`/`--text-file` flag only — one more flag to learn, and the `-`/`@file` idiom already exists on `sofar import`; (b) tolerant JSON parsing (JSON5, smart-quote repair) — hides the mangling instead of removing it and makes the log's validation weaker; (c) storing `supersedes` unqualified — repo.md and doctor cite qualified handles only (repo-memory-capture D2), an unqualified one would be ambiguous repo-wide; (d) deleting or rewriting the superseded memory — history is append-only.

payload.because: Round 1's stalls read `no session registered … (exit 1)` and nothing else, so a missing binary, a logged-out agent and a crashed hook all looked identical and cost the operator a transcript hunt. The adapters already buffer the stderr tail and the spawn error for their own use; carrying them onto the exit record is the cheapest path to `every launch failure names its cause`.
payload.chose: 1.6 drive diagnostics: the adapter exit record (SessionExit) carries `stderr_tail` (what the agent wrote to stderr, last chunk) and `spawn_error` (ENOENT and friends), both adapters fill them; the driver renders one `describeExit` line — exit code or signal, the spawn error, the last non-empty stderr line clipped — and puts it (a) on the progress line of every unresolved launch and every stall handoff, (b) in the run_stopped note for a stall stop (`last: …`), and (c) as an optional `detail` field on the stall/threshold handoff event so the cause is durable per session, not only in the driver's stderr. The handoff REASON is still read from the fold alone (D5) — detail annotates, never decides.
payload.over: (a) progress lines only — a detached run's stderr is not the record, and the next driver resumes from the record; (b) trusting the exit code or stderr to classify the handoff — D5 forbids it, and an agent that crashed after writing back still handed off on what the record shows; (c) appending a note_added per failed launch — record hygiene: a launch that registered no session files no handoff (D3), and a note would be a second event type saying the same thing.

payload.chose: 2.1 four levers, each a separate ablation arm (D5): (A) the digest ends its decisions block with one line naming the NEXT handles — `Next ids: D<n+1>, M<m+1>` — so a session can cite the decision or memory it is about to log without a fold or a get_state; (B) sofar_update_task returns bare {ok, event_id} on every status — the standing-constraint echo on `active` (drift-hardening 4.1) is dropped, superseding that lever; the constraints stay injected at SessionStart and enforced mechanically by the point-of-use guard (§Hooks); (C) sofar_end_session takes `tasks?: [{task_id, status, note?}]`, validated as a whole before any append and applied in order under the session before session_ended, returning `tasks_applied`; (D) the MCP server declares `instructions` (SDK initialize) telling a client with deferred tools to load the core five in ONE ToolSearch and to skip get_state after the hook injection; the CLAUDE.md block's DURING/BEFORE FINISHING lines say task changes may ride the write-back.
payload.over: (a) keeping the constraint echo but capping it — every echo repeats text the session already holds from SessionStart, and the guard hook is the enforcing half, so a capped echo is still pure repetition; (b) a separate sofar_batch tool — one more schema on every turn (2.4 is trimming the surface); (c) putting the next ids in tool responses only — the digest is read before the first write, which is when a session plans its citations; (d) instructions long enough to restate the protocol — the block already does, and instructions ride every initialize.

payload.because: Measured on this repo's records: decisions + rejected ledger are 34% of the r1-fixes digest (2,410 of 7,102 chars) and up to 4,300 chars on older records; every recent line's 280-char clip lands inside `chose` (5/5 here), so the rationale the line promises is already absent while the same `over` text is paid twice. drift-certification renders at exactly 10,000 chars, so its tail — Next ids and the read-back line — is what enforceStatusLimit cuts today; a count-capped index ends that. Handles on every line make citation possible without a fold, the same reason D10 added Next ids.
payload.chose: 2.2 digest dedupe, index-first: the two decision sections (Recent decisions ×5 at 280 chars, then a Rejected-approaches ledger of EVERY decision's `over`) become one index. (A) Recent window: `- [D<n>] <date> <chose ≤120> — over <over ≤90>` — handle first (the citation key), fields clipped separately so `over` always survives, `because` left to decisions.md (named in the header) instead of being the part the 280 clip cut anyway; a placeholder `(no alternative recorded)` renders no over clause. (B) A ruled decision whose rule rendered in Standing constraints above shows `(rule above)` and a 60-char chose — the constraint is its operative content, so the index stops restating it. (C) The ledger lists ONLY decisions older than the recent window (`Earlier rejected approaches — do NOT re-propose (N older)`), each `- [D<n>] <over ≤90>`, so no `over` text appears twice; ≤5 decisions → no ledger at all. Budgets unchanged elsewhere: rules verbatim, repo memory 1500, summary 1200, hard cap 10,000. PREDICT (bench-refresh D10): S2+ digest −25% chars with no C2/C3 loss; local proxy = this repo's 41 records with ≥2 sessions, mean 5,026 chars before. Each of A, B, C is measured on that corpus as its own arm (D5).
payload.over: (a) dropping the rejected ledger and keeping 5 × 280-char prose lines — the ledger is what carries C3 breadth once decisions age out of the window; (b) shrinking the whole line to 200 chars with the same `chose … over … — because` concatenation — the clip lands inside `chose` on every real record, so `over` and `because` vanish together; (c) a new get_state view or find output for decision detail — decisions.md is one read away on every host, and 2.4 is trimming the tool surface, not growing it; (d) cutting the write-back summary or repo memory budgets — neither duplicates anything, and the summary is the one text the previous session wrote for this one.

payload.because: Measured on this repo's records: of 182 consecutive-session pairs, the digest shares 0.8% of its bytes — the title only — because the per-session `Session:` line is line 3 and the `Git:` sha is line 5, ahead of a goal, four verbatim rules, 1,500 chars of repo memory and the phase list that do not change between sessions. Prompt caching matches prefixes, so bytes that never change belong before bytes that change every session; the gain is only realized when the host's own prefix (system prompt, CLAUDE.md, its git status) is also identical — same-sha restarts, parallel sessions, compaction re-fires — which is the honest bound on the prediction and why the local proxy measures the block alone.
payload.chose: 2.3 cache-stable digest layout, ordered by volatility: (1) static head — title, Goal, Standing constraints, Repo memory, Phases; (2) record-state sections — Progress/active/current/next task, Next action, parallel/stale/notes/blocked/concurrent lines, Last session, Driven, unwritten sessions, the decision index, Next ids; (3) a volatile tail — Adjacent records, the `Session:` line, the `Git:` line, and the hook notices (recent work elsewhere, closed banner, cold-resume advisory, shipping) which move INSIDE renderStatus as a `notices` option instead of a preface; (4) Read-back and footer stay last. The rejected ledger's cap reserve now counts the tail's real length, so the protocol tail still renders on heavy records. Nothing moves to UserPromptSubmit: the per-prompt path already carries the drift nudge and the landed line, and the shipping check is two git spawns that D6 keeps off that path. Supersedes placement only — every line keeps its wording and budget: BD43 (Session line near the top), record-integrity 4.1 (Git above Goal), session-orientation 2.2 (recent-work line leads), felt-cost 2.2 (advisory precedes the block), record-index 3.3 (adjacency last in the current block), commit-attribution 3.2 (shipping notice composed around the block). Byte-stability (felt-cost 1.2) is restated precisely: for identical state and options-minus-notices, the block is byte-identical up to the notices. PREDICT (bench-refresh D10): cache-creation tokens per session −15%; local proxy = the share of the block that is byte-identical between consecutive sessions of the same record, 0.8% before (182 pairs, every one diverging at line 3).
payload.over: (a) moving the Session id out of the block into a separate hook line after it — the same bytes at the same position, one more surface to teach; (b) leaving the notices as a preface and only reordering the block — the shipping notice renders on every session of an unpushed branch and is the first byte, so the reorder would buy nothing here; (c) sending staleness, notes and the read-back through UserPromptSubmit instead — they are state-derived and cost nothing, and the per-prompt path is budgeted at 100ms (D6); (d) dropping the Session line from the digest and relying on hook-registered adoption — start_session needs the id in the agent's hands, and 1.1 just put it on the unbound notice for the same reason.

payload.because: Codex and Cursor carry every MCP tool schema in every turn (round 1: ~3.5k tokens per turn, bench-refresh 1.4), and the three least-called tools — a review is per phase, a close is once, a find is occasional — are a third of the bytes. Each already has a CLI surface that every host can run, and Claude Code's deferred loading (D10's one-call core set) does not include them anyway. Descriptions were written as documentation; the SPEC and the payload reference hold the documentation, and the schema is paid per turn.
payload.chose: 2.4 tool surface in two arms (D5): (A) sofar_review, sofar_close_initiative and sofar_find leave the MCP tool list — CLI-first: `sofar review` prints the packet and now ends with the exact `sofar event append --type review_recorded --payload -` heredoc that records the verdict, `sofar close` closes (it already returns the overrides), `sofar find` traverses; the server instructions name the three commands; TOOL_NAMES/TOOL_DEFS shrink to nine and the MCP modules for the three are removed (applyClose stays, the CLI uses it). (B) Every remaining description is cut to its load-bearing sentence(s): the `initiative` property (repeated on 7 tools) drops to one clause, tool and property descriptions stop restating each other, and long prose (end_session's peer protocol, update_phase, remember, log_decision's guard grammar) keeps the rule and loses the essay. PREDICT (bench-refresh D10): MCP tool definitions 15,272 chars measured today (12 tools, name + description + inputSchema serialized; the plan's 14.8k was 0.32.0 before 2.1 added `tasks`) → ≤8,000; A and B measured separately.
payload.over: (a) trimming descriptions only and keeping 12 tools — the three schemas alone are 4,876 chars, so ≤8k is unreachable without dropping them; (b) a `sofar review --record` CLI flag — the convention dialect already records any event with a validated payload, and a second write path for one event type is what 1.3's payload reference exists to avoid; (c) keeping the three as MCP tools with one-line descriptions — the inputSchema is most of their size, and hosts without deferred tools pay it every turn; (d) dropping sofar_get_state instead — it is the one read an MCP-only host has when the injected block is missing.

Its corpus() appends two decisions back to back and expects the cursor one labelled D1; if both land in the same millisecond, ULID random bits can order the second first, so the label reads D2. payload.because: Measured on a synthetic 11 MB, 40,901-event log: fold 79 ms (read 6, decode 33, replay+derive 41), structuredClone of the folded state 0.6 ms, edges.slice 0 ms. A hook that folds twice pays ~158 ms; with the checkpoint the second fold is one applyEvent plus a finalize, a few ms. PREDICT (one arm, D5): post-tool and session-end hook fold time p50 −40% or better on a ~10 MB record (expected ≈ −45%); MCP tool calls in a long-lived server that append to an unchanged log fold zero times; projection bytes byte-identical to 0.32.0 on every conformance golden. Falls back to a full fold on every path the fast path cannot prove — a correction, an out-of-order id, a size or mtime mismatch — so a stale state is never served.
payload.chose: 2.7 single fold per append, exact: fold.ts splits foldLines into replayDecoded (the per-event loop, retained as a FoldCheckpoint: un-finalized state plus every side table — blockNotes, edges, seenSessions, orphan candidates, guard cache, voided set, last id, line count) and finalizeFold (structuredClone the state, then task_files, activity, deriveCurrent, orphans, unregistered — the post-loop as today, on the clone only). appendToCheckpoint(cp, line) applies ONE appended event through the same loop body when it is envelope-valid, not a correction, and its id ≥ the last replayed id; anything else returns null and the caller refolds. ToolContext.foldState caches {size, mtimeMs, checkpoint} per slug (LRU 8): a stat that matches serves finalizeFold; appendAndProject advances the checkpoint with the line it just wrote when the post-append stat equals cached size + line bytes, else drops it. Projection bytes are untouched: the state a hit returns is deep-equal to a fresh fold by construction, pinned by a property test over prefixes, corrections and out-of-order ids.
payload.over: (a) caching only the decoded lines — parse is 33 of 79 ms on an 11 MB log, replay 41, so the second fold would still cost half; (b) replacing the pre-append fold with a raw-line scan (registrationIn-style) for registration and ended checks — diverges from the fold on voided or invalid events, and session-end still needs the fold; (c) deferring projection regeneration — changes when projections are written, which the SPEC's per-append contract and the record's settle-on-commit behaviour rely on; (d) a persisted state cache on disk — a second store that can desync from the log (record-integrity D1).
